text:
Sophia: Heads-up: seeing KV cache memory steadily grow on long chat sessions (>65k tokens) on mixed H100/RTX pools, not reclaiming. Appears correlated with eviction order differences when pages move over NVLink vs PCIe. Anyone seen this? :eyes:
Liam: Which deployment + model? quick logs would help.
Sophia: repro on dedicated-dynamic-h100-rtx (mixed queue) with gptx-13b-fp16. Pasting the kvcache tail from the failing run: 
```
[2026-06-01T14:02:11Z] kvcache: pages_in_use=1248 pages_free=32 total_pages=1280
[2026-06-01T14:02:11Z] evict_batch: gpu0->gpu1 via NVLink: candidates=[p102,p203,p87]
[2026-06-01T14:02:11Z] evict: freed p203 (owner=gpu1)
[2026-06-01T14:02:11Z] alloc: reinsert p203 -> gpu0 (reuse hit)
[2026-06-01T14:02:11Z] kvcache: pages_in_use=1251 pages_free=29
```
Sophia: page gets freed on gpu1, then reinserted on gpu0 shortly after — we end up with NP>total_pages over time (not exact double-free but logical leak / fragmentation).
Omar: I ran a microbench: same pattern on A100+H100 mix if we enable cross_gpu_reuse heuristics. If I turn that knob off, usage stabilizes. Might be ordering/races on the eviction ack path.
Jess: FWIW I tracked a perf/regression graph. After kernel selection change 1c2f8b (fused-attn-v2 default tile=128) we started prefetching different stride lengths which changes which KV pages are touched together. That increases page churn and the cross-gpu reuse heuristic makes more page movement -> exposes ordering bug. Link to flamegraph: https://internal.redwood/fg/1765 (private)
Liam: Sounds plausible. NVLink vs PCIe paths have different round-trip ordering for async DMA completions. If eviction frees on remote GPU before local reuse sees the free, we can reassign stale page ids into different owners and leak hole fragments.
Sophia: Repro script is small, can run locally on the mixed test pool: 
```bash
./scripts/long_ctx_repro.sh --model gptx-13b-fp16 --seq 70000 --threads 32 --cross-gpu-reuse on
```
Sophia: kill -9 the worker after ~10 min to capture a snapshot, then run `./tools/kv-inspect dump-pagetable --gpu 0 --format short`
Liam: We should add more strict checks in debug builds: assert that page.owner isn't reused while page.flags==FREE_PENDING and add a counter for pending-remote-acks. That would help catch the window.
Jess: I'll open a small PR to add the debug assert + a config flag to disable cross-gpu-reuse at runtime (rollout: default true on prod, but off in private schedulers until fixed). PR will also surface per-gpu pending-ack stats in /metrics/kvcache. Assigning @Liam for review. :+1:
Omar: Quick mitigation we used in the past: batch evictions and wait for completion ack before allowing remote reinserts. Costs a bit of latency but solves growth. We should measure tail latency impact.
Sophia: For the immediate on-call mitigation, infra-bot can flip the config on the mixed queue to disable cross-gpu moves.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: jobs/1765432190-disable-crossgpu-reuse on queue dedicated-dynamic-h100-rtx at 2026-06-01T14:10Z. Outcome: disabled.
Liam: Also adding note: this race only surfaces with the new kernel tiling because it changes the hot-set locality -> more cross-gpu page boundary touches. If we can change eviction_batch_size down (8->4) it reduces churn too. We should test both knobs.
Jess: I'll add a small benchmark in the PR that toggles eviction_batch_size and measures 95/99 latency and peak mem.
Omar: Repro tip: set `RUNTIME_KV_DEBUG=1` to get page table dumps and `KV_EVICT_DELAY=50ms` to exaggerate timing window.
Sophia: Thanks folks — pretty high priority. Leaving notes in ops runbook and adding a brief to the release notes about the kernel tile impact. :thinking:
Liam: OK next steps: (1) Jess PR for asserts/flags/metrics, (2) run mitigation on mixed queue (infra-bot done), (3) measure perf impact of batching vs wait-for-acks, (4) permanent fix to reorder remote-free/reinsert path.
Jess: Will do.
Sophia: Great, I'll attach one captured pagetable dump to the ticket.
